title.narrative: Giving for Change programme - Brazil

description.narrative: The aim of Giving for Change – funded by the Dutch government’s ‘Power of Voices’ programme – is to foster local giving as an expression of voice, civic participation, solidarity and dissent. The programme will build evidence around new thinking, approaches and leadership that support community philanthropy development. Giving for Change will promote community philanthropy as a strategy for achieving community-led development by increasing local ownership, buy-in and claiming of rights, and by challenging the notion that development is something that is “done to” communities by external actors. Against a global background of shrinking civic space, Giving for Change will encourage civil society organizations, including and especially human rights organizations, to value and adopt local resource mobilization as a form of constituency building, and as a way to strengthen their position as legitimate champions and defenders of diverse causes, with strong roots in the communities they serve. #ShiftThePower. While the programme will maintain an explicit focus on strengthening rights and claiming capacities of communities in relation to public government structures, another dimension of it relates specifically to challenging power dynamics, and establishing more equitable practices within the international development system itself. Programme activities will include action research, trainings and grants to stimulate local giving, which will be led in each country by national anchor institutions. The role of consortium members will be to help “weave” dialogue, learning and exchange across the programme itself, as well beyond to global platforms and audiences as part of larger advocacy and influencing efforts to transform development and philanthropic practice.

The programme in Brazil will focus on community based initiatives, representing and targeting most marginalized groups; women and girls, black people, LGBTQI+ population, indigenous and traditional populations. They are not particularly targeted by the mainstream social investment ecosystem in Brazil. The focus at national level will be: - Changed mindset of relevant stakeholders on the value of community philanthropy and the #ShiftThePower agenda; - More resources channeled to local communities and to social justice and human rights CSAs (particularly to community-based CSAs, and to specific targets such as black community, women and girls, indigenous, quilombola and traditional populations, and LGBTIQ community). Different donors, including foundations and companies are targeted, including a specific event for the ecumenical movement in Brazil. - Increased public support for and resources channeled to local communities and to social justice and human rights CSAs, because of a broader acknowledgment within Brazilian society of the role of CSO and HROs in relation to democracy; a counter-narrative in the context of de-legimatization of civil society by government and conservative sectors.

The State Legislative Assembly unanimously approved the creation of the State Week of Awareness about the rights of the category: Bill (345/23) authored by state deputy Luciano Cartaxo (PT), which adds to the Paraíba's official calendar is the State Week of Awareness on the Rights of Domestic Workers, to be celebrated annually in the week of April 27th. The approval took place at the Ordinary Session of the Legislative Assembly of Paraíba (ALPB), which took place on November 21st in the city of Patos, Sertão Paraíba (action resulting from support for a small project). Others was : - the creation of the Hotline service ; - the reactivation of an interinstitutional Public Security Working Group for the LGBT population, after a meeting with the Secretary of Public Security and demonstrations and a manifesto denouncing that Piauí does not have public policies for the LGBT population, carried out by Grupo Matizes, a member of the CoP that works to defend lesbian women and LGBT people in Piauí. - They also managed to change, with the Presidency of the Piauí Identification Institute, the forms for issuing the General Identification Records (RG), which still limited the filling of the father and mother category, causing restrictions on same-sex couples. - Together with the Municipal Education Department of Teresina, they also managed to change the registration form for municipal schools in the city of Teresina to include social names for trans people and in the "gender" part to include female/male/other

Conversations are ongoing with mapped organizations to engage them, aiming for their potential inclusion in the Network in the upcoming years. CESE on the other hand added 4 more groups to be involved in CoP activities in 2023.

4 additional CoPs
5 CoPs have been established in 2021

In 2023, Comuá Network has launched one new CoP on Institutional Development. As of now, the Network has 4 active communities of practices: Philanthropy and Democracy, Knowledge Production, Communications and Narratives and Institutional Development. Both the Monitoring and Evaluation and Grantmaking and Resource Mobilization have been merged, respectively, with the Institutional Development and Philanthropy and Democracy CoPs.
